status: Research architecture, not an automatic legal decision engine

levels.daruriyyat: Essentials: without which religious and worldly order may be gravely impaired
levels.hajiyyat: Needs: mitigate hardship and allow stable functioning
levels.tahsiniyyat: Refinements: proper conduct, quality, excellence and cultivated manners

cross_axis.establish: Positive formation and construction of a required good
cross_axis.protect: Safeguard against actual or anticipated loss or corruption

warning: The five classical necessities are not the entirety of religious life. Broader aims and strategic programmes are explicitly labelled and not all legally equivalent. A programme linked to a maqṣad is not thereby farḍ kifāya.

aims.name: Religion and revealed guidance
aims.scope: A core field of the five necessities
aims.formation: Cultivate sound belief, worship, knowledgeable practice, sincerity and the capacity to transmit religious knowledge.
aims.safeguarding: Address ignorance, misrepresentation, loss of qualified teachers, coercion and practices undermining religious responsibility.
aims.caution: The full reality of knowing God and spiritual excellence is not exhausted by a juridical safeguarding category.

aims.name: Life and bodily security
aims.scope: A core field of the five necessities
aims.formation: Develop competent medicine, appropriate care, reliable infrastructure and conditions of human safety.
aims.safeguarding: Prevent avoidable death, serious illness, violence, unsafe service and acute deprivation.
aims.caution: Distinguish health outcomes from professional headcounts and official targets.

aims.name: Intellect, knowledge and sound judgment
aims.scope: A core field of the five necessities
aims.formation: Educate, cultivate reasoning and deliberation, transmit expertise, and support intellectual institutions.
aims.safeguarding: Resist falsehood, avoidable ignorance, impairments and systems that degrade independent judgment.
aims.caution: A philosophical programme of intellectual renewal is a proposed positive application, not a direct claim that every project is legally necessary.

aims.name: Family, continuity and responsible care
aims.scope: A core field of the five necessities
aims.formation: Sustain family responsibilities, upbringing, education, intergenerational support and secure households.
aims.safeguarding: Prevent neglect, insecurity, exploitation and conditions obstructing the care of dependants.
aims.caution: Do not identify flourishing with demographic or economic maximisation.

aims.name: Property, trustworthy exchange and stewardship
aims.scope: A core field of the five necessities
aims.formation: Make lawful livelihoods possible, protect the reliability of transactions, support honest crafts and durable institutions.
aims.safeguarding: Prevent fraud, unjust taking, corrupt procurement and destruction of essential resources.
aims.caution: Growth of wealth is not the final human end; lawful means, distribution and formation matter.

aims.name: Spiritual and moral formation
aims.scope: Islamic life and ethics beyond a five-item legal checklist
aims.formation: Cultivate worship, remembrance, humility, sound habits, discernment and virtues practiced in family and public life.
aims.safeguarding: Guard against using professional success or institutional power as substitutes for sincerity and responsibility.
aims.caution: No metric, job ranking or outcome indicator can establish a person's nearness to God.

aims.name: Justice, trust and right governance
aims.scope: General public aims discussed in later maqāṣid and social-order literature
aims.formation: Build reliable adjudication, trustworthy administration, equitable access and accountable institutions.
aims.safeguarding: Resist domination, corruption, concealment of harms and arbitrary exclusion.
aims.caution: A proposed governance model must be justified through evidence and juristic reasoning; not every reform is obligatory.

aims.name: Civilizational and institutional flourishing
aims.scope: General social-order and reform aims, particularly developed by Ibn ʿĀshūr
aims.formation: Enable households, professions, schools, crafts, governments and associations to cooperate in legitimate goods.
aims.safeguarding: Protect institutional continuity, just public order and access to essential provision.
aims.caution: Growth, scale and control are not equivalent to the good of the people who inhabit institutions.

aims.name: Intellectual and religious renewal
aims.scope: Proposed civilizational programme informed by tajdīd/iḥyāʾ literature
aims.formation: Renew understanding through sound scholarship, critical reconstruction, curriculum, living teaching and serious engagement with contemporary questions.
aims.safeguarding: Prevent loss of competent transmission, shallow imitation, fragmentation and ideology replacing scholarship.
aims.caution: A general mandate to renewal does not establish that any particular translation, school or curriculum is binding.

aims.name: Ecological and material stewardship
aims.scope: A proposed application under the classical necessities, public benefit and responsible use of the earth
aims.formation: Support water, land, food systems, healthy settlements and intergenerational care of common resources.
aims.safeguarding: Prevent pollution, depletion, unsafe infrastructure and damage that undermines necessary human provision.
aims.caution: Not presented as a historically unanimous sixth canonical necessity.

programmes.name: Form the next generation of qualified scholars
programmes.why: Textual archives alone do not reproduce judgment, character or teaching competence. Formative relationships and supervised progression matter.
firstSteps: Map the disciplines and stages of qualification required
Identify competent teachers and gaps in succession
Pilot supervised study routes, then evaluate outcomes
tests: Independently assess actual competence
Track sustained teaching and supervision
Document the limits of accreditation and self-reported achievements
programmes.status: Research programme proposal; no national shortage demonstrated

programmes.name: Primary texts, editions, translations and access
programmes.why: Scholarly traditions need reliable access to their sources and methods, not only isolated quotations or unverified digital transcriptions.
firstSteps: Identify genuine gaps in text access and edition quality
Develop verified bilingual reading materials
Create responsible pathways back to Arabic and manuscript evidence
tests: Document provenance and variant readings
Distinguish critical collation from working edition
Test whether readers genuinely improve understanding
programmes.status: Research programme proposal; priority depends on demonstrated textual and educational need

programmes.name: Integrated curricula in the intellectual sciences
programmes.why: A course list is not enough: learning should progress from foundational reasoning to mature inquiry and responsible action.
firstSteps: Define the human and disciplinary ends before outcomes
Map prerequisites across logic, language, philosophy, fiqh and contemporary disciplines
Pilot teaching, assessment and longitudinal formation
tests: Separate genuine understanding from credentials and volume of content
Assess whether programmes remain faithful to their subject
Monitor unintended professional or sectarian effects
programmes.status: Research programme proposal; Malaysian IIUM studies give models and critical cautions

programmes.name: Disciplined engagement with contemporary discourses
programmes.why: Neither polemical rejection nor uncritical import of modern theories secures understanding. Traditions require competent engagement with the strongest arguments and evidence.
firstSteps: Select questions from science, law, technology, economics and politics
Recover classical principles and their interpretive methods
Develop rigorous exchanges, critiques and teachable syntheses
tests: Represent opponents fairly
Check claims with field specialists
Record unresolved issues and competing interpretations

programmes.name: Renew living legal discernment and institutional jurisprudence
programmes.why: Law must distinguish stable norms from variable institutional means. Modern questions require qualified method, not merely a blueprint transferred from one era.
firstSteps: Collate madhhab positions and primary legal reasoning
Study contemporary institutions and actual consequences
Produce responsibly reviewed issue dossiers
tests: Identify disagreement and legal authority
Distinguish fatwā from research hypothesis
Assess whether solutions are socially and legally viable
programmes.status: Research agenda requiring qualified juristic review

programmes.name: Ethical formation in everyday work and institutions
programmes.why: The value of an occupation cannot be inferred from its output; habits, intention, care, justice and responsibilities shape the person's actual life.
firstSteps: Develop realistic studies of ordinary work and care
Pair traditional ethical readings with supervised reflection
Study institutional conditions that encourage or damage good practice
tests: Do not score inner sincerity
Avoid coercive spirituality or intrusive personal data
Attend to burdens on carers and workers
programmes.status: Formative programme, not a measure of spiritual rank

programmes.name: Household sufficiency, care and intergenerational formation
programmes.why: Livelihood security, family duties, education and care form one ecology rather than isolated services.
firstSteps: Identify household obligations and actual welfare standards
Map available services without assuming all needs require a new NGO
Evaluate support to existing caregivers and dependants
tests: Preserve household dignity and privacy
Avoid confusing income data with benefit adequacy
Identify unintended dependency or exclusion
programmes.status: Institutional programme; specific location evidence required

programmes.name: Justice, public trust and institutional capacity
programmes.why: Hospitals, schools, religious institutions and public services depend on governance, financial integrity, staffing and public trust.
firstSteps: Document which functions institutions actually fulfil
Assess accountability, access and alternatives
Train practitioners in governance and stewardship
tests: No presumption that more institutions are always better
Compare organisational arrangements
Record tradeoffs and contested mandates

programmes.name: Technology, human agency and the conditions of knowledge
programmes.why: Digital systems alter knowing, teaching, judgment, privacy and institutional authority, beyond their immediate technical benefits.
firstSteps: Develop conceptual and empirical studies of technological mediation
Review independent AI safety and governance research
Test systems for effects on learning, work, privacy and reasoning
tests: Separate claims of catastrophic harm from verified mechanisms
Avoid equating adoption with progress
Assess epistemic independence and effects on attention
programmes.status: Research programme, with contested normative and empirical questions

programmes.name: Revive craftsmanship and trustworthy livelihoods
programmes.why: Work can form competence and character while producing necessary goods. Vocational excellence is broader than salary or predicted impact.
firstSteps: Map essential and qualitative crafts in a locality
Study apprenticeships and demand before proposing new programmes
Develop dignified training and responsible enterprise
outputs: Assessment of actual access to work
tests: Avoid romanticising hereditary caste or inequitable labour
Test livelihood viability
Do not require every profession to carry a grand civilizational slogan

programmes.name: Stewardship of essential resources and settlements
programmes.why: Social life requires stable access to food, water, shelter and functioning infrastructures, including across disruptions.
firstSteps: Assess actual infrastructure and supply chains
Study failure modes and alternatives
Prioritise maintenance and local competence as well as new construction
tests: Verify physical risks and local data
Include external and long-term harms
Separate relief appeals from independently verified deficits

programmes.name: Historical and comparative civilizational learning
programmes.why: A tradition capable of understanding itself and others needs history, languages, comparative sources and careful interpretation of institutional change.
firstSteps: Develop comparative studies of historical social arrangements
Investigate non-Muslim traditions without presuming doctrinal identity
Present the findings as accessible scholarly and curricular materials
tests: Do not flatten differences among traditions
Distinguish historical evidence from metaphysical interpretation
Seek independent critique of major claims
